ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: the diagram labeled ethanol shows a very short alcohol structure with an O-H group, while the diagram labeled octane shows a much longer straight chain of eight carbon atoms with hydrogens attached. Reasoning: the given boiling points are 78°C for ethanol and 125°C for octane, so octane requires more energy to separate its molecules. The long octane chain has more electrons and more surface area than the much smaller ethanol molecule, making its temporary dipoles/London dispersion forces stronger. Therefore, octane has the higher boiling point because its temporary dipoles are stronger than those in ethanol.
